reason: The provided sources contain more than enough facts and claims to support a surprising 45-second story with well over 10 atomic claims backed by at least two distinct sources.
story: In 2025, biotechnology company Colossal Biosciences announced they brought back the extinct dire wolf by creating three genetically modified pups named Romulus, Remus, and Khaleesi. Rather than cloning from tissue or injecting ancient DNA directly, scientists extracted endothelial progenitor cells from modern gray wolf blood samples. Using CRISPR technology, they made 20 edits across 14 genes to produce dire wolf traits like a pale coat, larger body size, wider head, and a powerful shoulder structure. The edited nuclei were placed into denucleated ova, and the resulting embryos were implanted into surrogate domestic dogs. Born via planned cesarean sections, the pups have exhibited wild wolf behaviors, such as howling from two weeks old and keeping their distance from humans. However, independent experts and the IUCN argue the animals are merely hybrid gray wolves rather than true de-extinct dire wolves, pointing out that dire wolves diverged millions of years ago.
angle: Scientists did not resurrect the dire wolf using ancient DNA; instead, they made just 20 edits to 14 genes in living gray wolves, sparking a fierce debate over whether the animals are true de-extinction or just genetically modified hybrids.

claims.claim: Colossal Biosciences announced the creation of three genetically modified gray wolf pups intended to mimic the extinct dire wolf, named Romulus, Remus, and Khaleesi.
The dire wolf species went extinct approximately 10,000 to 13,000 years ago.
No ancient dire wolf DNA was actually spliced into the gray wolf's genome; instead, existing genes were rewritten.
Scientists made 20 targeted edits across 14 genes in gray wolf endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) sourced from blood draws.
The genomic blueprint came from two ancient samples: a 13,000-year-old tooth from Sheridan Pit, Ohio, and a 72,000-year-old ear bone from American Falls, Idaho.
The modified nuclei were transferred into denucleated egg cells, developed into embryos, and implanted into surrogate domestic dog mixes.
Romulus and Remus were born on October 1, 2024, and their sister Khaleesi was born on January 30, 2025.
All three wolf pups were delivered via planned cesarean section to minimize birthing complications.
By six months of age, the male wolves measured nearly 4 feet long and weighed 80 pounds.
The pups began howling at around two weeks of age.
Independent experts and the IUCN dispute the claim, arguing the animals are genetically modified hybrid gray wolves rather than true resurrected dire wolves.
Dire wolves diverged from gray wolves between 2.5 and 6 million years ago and belong to an entirely separate genus.

disputed: Whether the created animals qualify as true 'de-extinction' or are merely 'gray wolves with 20 edits' (the script should attribute the hybrid/modified label to independent scientists and the IUCN while noting Colossal's functional proxy definition).
